sources.title: J. F. Adams, Stable Homotopy and Generalised Homology
sources.locator: Chapter 2, construction from a cohomology theory and Example 2.2, printed pp. 174–179; Chapter 6(v), connective K-theory, printed pp. 245–246; Proposition 16.6 and its proof, printed pp. 391–393
sources.read_evidence: The live 432-page Rochester PDF was fetched and extracted. Chapter 2, printed pp. 174–179, constructs the Omega-spectrum associated to a cohomology theory and identifies complex K-theory's spectrum as the BU-spectrum. Chapter 6(v), printed pp. 245–246, defines bu→K by vanishing negative stable homotopy and isomorphism in nonnegative stems and states bu^0(X)=K^0(X). Proposition 16.6, printed pp. 391–393, identifies the first bu (modern ku) k-invariant as the nonzero operation δ₂Sq², supplies the H³(H), H⁶(K(Z,3);Z), and H⁶(SU;Z) facts used to distinguish it from zero, and fixes its normalization with the Bott cofiber long exact sequence. Adams does not supply the skeletal/Postnikov exact-couple comparison, which is proved in the local bridge lemma.

alternatives.argument: Superseded by the live source. Proposition 16.6 explicitly identifies the two possible first bu k-invariants as 0 and δ₂Sq², supplies the H³(H), H⁶(K(Z,3);Z), and H⁶(SU;Z) facts that force the nonzero choice, and uses the Bott cofiber long exact sequence to fix the normalization. Under the local conventions this is β_ZSq²ρ₂.

Superseded by the live sources plus the proof-bearing local bridge. That bridge identifies the bundle-defined K-groups with the KU-prespectrum groups, compares the nonpositive KU rows with Adams's connective cover, and proves from the exact-couple local-lift rule and cellular lifting obstruction that d₃ is the first representing-space Postnikov invariant. The theorem treats p=0 componentwise by AHSS naturality and transports all rows by Bott periodicity.
